title: Loops into a kernel
starter:
%x = buffer 64 dtype=f32 slot=0
%o = buffer 64 dtype=f32 slot=1
# o = 3x + 1 for 64 elements, as 4 blocks of 16 threads. Make %b the blocks and %t the threads.
%b = range 4
%t = range 16
%m = mul %b 16
%i = add %m %t
%xv = shrink %x %i shape=[]
%xe = load %xv
%y = mul %xe 3.0
%z = add %y 1.0
%ov = shrink %o %i shape=[]
%s = store %ov %z
%et = end %s %t
%eb = end %et %b
%o1 = after %o %eb
hints: The offset b·16 + t is already a unique number: 16 is more than 15, the most t can add.
The result doesn't change, only how it would run: 4 blocks of 16 threads.

answer.code:
%x = buffer 64 dtype=f32 slot=0
%o = buffer 64 dtype=f32 slot=1
# o = 3x + 1 for 64 elements, as 4 blocks of 16 threads.
%b = range 4 axis=global
%t = range 16 axis=local
%m = mul %b 16
%i = add %m %t
%xv = shrink %x %i shape=[]
%xe = load %xv
%y = mul %xe 3.0
%z = add %y 1.0
%ov = shrink %o %i shape=[]
%s = store %ov %z
%et = end %s %t
%eb = end %et %b
%o1 = after %o %eb
answer.explain: On a GPU each value of %b is a block and each value of %t a thread in it. The offset 16b + t gives every thread of every block its own element, which the rule checks as a mixed-radix number. run and the CPU render treat it as the same loops as before, so the bits can't change.
